← Auth MAU Pricing Calculator

How to choose an auth provider by monthly active users

Put your user count and growth rate into the calculator to price Clerk, Auth0, AWS Cognito, Firebase, Supabase Auth and WorkOS side by side. These are the questions to settle before you trust the answer.

When does authentication become expensive?

Most hosted providers are free below a user count and then charge per monthly active user. The jump is in the pricing model, not the user count itself: a provider that is free to 50,000 users can cost nothing where another charges hundreds of dollars a month.

What counts as a monthly active user?

Vendors define it differently: a user who signs in, a user who refreshes a token, or any user with an active session in the month. Read each definition before comparing, because the same app can have a different MAU count under each.

What usually costs more than the per-user line?

Enterprise SSO and SAML connections, SMS multi-factor codes, B2B organization features, custom domains and support plans. A cheap per-user rate can still produce an expensive invoice once one enterprise customer asks for SAML.

Should I pick the cheapest provider at my user count today?

Not on price alone. Compare the 12-month spend under your growth rate, check how hard it is to migrate users out later, and confirm the free plan includes the features you need in production.

Enter your monthly active users and growth rate. Get Clerk, Auth0, AWS Cognito, Firebase, Supabase Auth and WorkOS priced side by side, the 12-month spend, and the user counts where the cheapest provider changes — before you build on one and find out at 50,000 users.

Prefer a CLI, or want a budget gate in CI?

node cli.mjs compare --mau 40000 --growth 8
node cli.mjs compare --mau 150000 --provider clerk --budget 500   # exit 1 over budget
node cli.mjs crossover

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: how to choose an auth provider by MAU.

Common questions

Does this read my auth provider account?

No. It uses only the monthly active user count you type and rate cards you can edit. It cannot see your plan, add-ons, contract or invoice. Treat every figure as a way to compare options, never as what you will be charged.

Where do the prices come from?

They are approximate public list prices as best known in 2025, shown with an as-of line, and every number is editable. Vendors change packaging often and define a monthly active user differently, so check each vendor's pricing page before deciding.

What is not included?

Enterprise SSO and SAML connections, SMS multi-factor authentication, B2B organizations, custom domains, support plans and committed-use discounts. These are often the real bill, so use this to compare the per-user line, not to forecast the whole invoice.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The page calculates in your browser and sends nothing. The CLI reads local files and makes no network call.
